messages.subject: no x y coordinates in shape properties of polygon
parts:
Hello,

I plan to use Distance to design line surveys to determine the key areas =
of habitat of a community of common dolphins that we regularly find close=
to shore in Port Phillip. I have managed to create two shapefiles of the=
areas I intend to cover during my vessel surveys in ESRI=E2=80=99s ArcMa=
p from a shapefile of Port Phillip.=20=20

I have imported the survey area shapefiles into Distance as described for=
the Mexico project by copying the files and renaming them in the datafol=
der. As suggested, I have also created an additional field =E2=80=98Link=
ID=E2=80=99 (long integer) in ArcCatalog. Once in Distance I can open and=
view each of the shapefiles as a correctly projected map in the map tab.=
The shapefiles use GDA 94 and transverse mercatore coordinates as per t=
he original map and are the setting used as the default in Distance.=20=20=


My problem arises when working with the file in the datatab. If I open t=
he shape properties dialog by double clicking the blank shape field type =
there are no x and y coordinates listed and no vertices although the file=
is recognised as a polygon. Without the x y coordinates I am unable to =
produce coverage girds and consequently cannot produce my desired line tr=
ansects. I am using ArcView and do not have access to ArcInfo to be able=
to be able to convert my shapefile to vertices that can be cut and paste=
directly into the shape properties dialog window. Is there a way to obta=
in the x and y coordinates?=20

Thank you in advance.

Sue Mason
PhD student=20
Curtin University

messages.subject: Re: no x y coordinates in shape properties of polygon
parts:
Hey,
I do not fully understand your question:
do you want to add x and y ?
If so, there is GME (former Hawths tools) or in ArcToolbox (Table Managemen=
t)
to do so.
But polygons do not have a single pair x and y though.

However, I went through your problem myself earlier, and all worked fine.
So perhaps I missing your goal and/or question ?

Otherwise, check with GME and for lattices and griddings (much easier there=
).
Clearly, DS is NOT a GIS ...

Very best
F.

EWHALE lab
